chain/chain: Often one function feeds another. Here x goes in and u comes out, where u is three x plus one.
chain/feed: Then u feeds a second function: z is u squared.
chain/vals: At x equals one, u is four, and z is sixteen. How fast does z change when x is nudged?
local/du: Each link has its own local slope. u is three x plus one, so u moves three times as fast as x.
local/dz: z is u squared, whose slope is two u. At u equals four, that is eight.
local/nudge: Now nudge x by zero point zero one. u moves three times that, zero point zero three. And z moves eight times that, zero point two four.
local/mult: So z moves three times eight, twenty four times as fast as x. That is the chain rule: multiply the local slopes.
back/longer: A chain can be as long as you like. Here x feeds u, u feeds v, and v feeds a last function, L. Each link has a local slope.
back/back: Start at the end and walk backwards, multiplying as you go: a half, times minus two is minus one, times three is minus three.
back/backprop: So a nudge to x moves L minus three times as much. And the walk finds more on the way: the slope of L with respect to v and to u as well.
